root_cause.text: The smb3_reconfigure() function fails to free and securely erase dynamically allocated password buffers (new_password and new_password2) when an error occurs in smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords(), resulting in both memory leak and information disclosure of sensitive credential data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds two kfree_sensitive() calls in the error handling path of smb3_reconfigure() immediately after the mutex_unlock() and before the return statement. The original code at lines 1139-1142 would return directly upon smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords() failure without deallocating the newly allocated password buffers, which were created earlier in the function but never freed in this error path. The use of kfree_sensitive() (rather than kfree()) is critical because it overwrites the memory with zeros before freeing, preventing sensitive password data from remaining in freed memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces proper memory management for password buffers in smb3_reconfigure(). The vulnerable construct described in the root cause (failure to free and securely erase new_password and new_password2 on error) is NOT present in this code. Instead, the code demonstrates correct handling: (1) new_password and new_password2 are allocated early (lines 981-995), (2) if new_password2 allocation fails, new_password is freed with kfree_sensitive() before returning -ENOMEM (lines 989-991), (3) the mutex is locked before password updates to prevent races (line 1003), (4) smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords() is called first to sync passwords safely (lines 1010-1011), and (5) only after successful allocation and sync do the passwords get committed to ses struct (lines 1017-1025). The code properly handles all error paths with kfree_sensitive() calls. This is a fix-introducing commit, not a bug-introducing one.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit INTRODUCES the fix for the vulnerability rather than containing the bug. The vulnerability root cause describes a failure to free password buffers when errors occur in smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords(). In this commit, the code properly handles memory cleanup: (1) new_password and new_password2 are allocated before calling smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords() at lines 983-997; (2) if smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords() returns an error at line 1009, the function returns -ENOMEM without leaking the allocated buffers because they haven't been assigned to ses->password/password2 yet; (3) the new_password and new_password2 buffers are only committed to ses struct AFTER the sync function succeeds (lines 1014-1021); (4) within smb3_sync_session_ctx_passwords() itself, if kstrdup for password2 fails at line 939, it properly cleans up the password field at lines 940-941 before returning -ENOMEM. The mutex protection and proper ordering of allocations before assignments prevents both the memory leak and information disclosure issues described in the vulnerability root cause.
